name: Riverscape Restoration Initiative
summary: Grants for low-tech, process-based and beaver-based restoration of streams and watersheds in the arid southwestern United States and northern Mexico, with smaller grants for capacity and landowner engagement.

amount.note: Implementation grants are $50,000 to $100,000; capacity grants go up to $25,000 and engagement grants up to $7,500.

eligibility.rule: Is a registered nonprofit, civil society organisation or Native American tribe
Is in the target area: Utah, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico or northern Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila or Nuevo León

documents: Proposal cover sheet with project, contact and summary
Explanation of activities and expected outcomes

status.quote: The deadline for proposals is March 31, 2026.

deadline.quote: The deadline for proposals is March 31, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: Proposals may be submitted by registered nonprofit organizations, civil society organizations, and Native American tribes in the geographic area described above.

geography.quote: improve the resilience of watersheds in arid and semi-arid regions of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico

access.quote: Email completed proposal as a PDF or Word document to Jennifer Gooden at jennifer@biophiliafoundation.org.

amount.quote: Implementation: Grants of $50,000 to $100,000 are available for projects that implement low-tech, process-based, and/or beaver-based restoration of upland streams and watersheds.

consortium_required.quote: Proposals may be submitted by a single entity or partnerships of multiple entities.

eligibility.quote: registered nonprofit organizations, civil society organizations, and Native American tribes
The target geography for these grants includes: • Utah, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico • The northern border regions of Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, and Nuevo León.

documents.quote: Cover sheet with name and location of project, name and contact information for primary contact person, and 2-4 sentence summary of the proposal 2. Description of problem(s) to be addressed and the factors that led to the problem(s) 3. Planned activities, including timeline and budget

Explanation of how the planned activities will address the problem and the expected outcomes for the environment, wildlife, and people 5. Risks associated with the project 6. List of stakeholders directly and indirectly affected by the project and how they have been or will be included in planning and decision making
